children.name: Petrosavia sakuraii  J.J.Sm. ex Steenis
children.description: thumbPetrosavia sakuraii, one of three species in the genus Petrosavia, is a monocotyledonous plant first described by Tomitaro Makino in 1903 (see illustration), distributed in eastern and south-eastern Asia.

children.name: Petrosavia sinii  Gagnep.
children.description: A small mycoheterotrophic (non-green) herb 4-10 cm tall, pale yellow and glabrous, with a scaly rhizome, a slender stem bearing small membranous scale-leaves, and a raceme of 7-12 tiny flowers whose perianth is adnate for about half its length to the ovary. In China it is recorded only from bamboo forests at ~1000 m in east-central Guangxi (Dayao Shan). Family Petrosaviaceae.

children.name: Petrosavia stellaris Becc.
children.description: The type species of the genus, a holomycotrophic (non-photosynthetic) rhizomatous geophyte in the monocot family Petrosaviaceae. Its native range spans southern Vietnam through Malesia, where it grows primarily in the wet tropical biome, typically on the shaded floor of humid forests.

children.name: Japonolirion osense Nakai
children.description: Japonolirion is a genus of plants in the family Petrosaviaceae. There is only one known species, Japonolirion osense, endemic to Japan.
